metadata.title: Applications of graph containers in the Boolean lattice
metadata.authors: J. Balogh, A. Treglown, A.Z. Wagner

nodes.name: Boolean lattice $\mathcal{P}(n)$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{P}(n)$ denotes the power set of $[n]:=\{1,\dots,n\}$, partially ordered by inclusion.

nodes.name: Antichain
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(n)$ is an antichain if for any $A,B\in\mathcal{A}$ with $A\subseteq B$ we have $A=B$.

nodes.name: $(p,q)$-tilted Sperner family
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(n)$ is a $(p,q)$-tilted Sperner family if it does not contain distinct $A,B$ with $q|A\setminus B|=p|B\setminus A|$.

nodes.name: Subcube spanned by $A$ and $B$
nodes.statement: Given $A,B\subseteq[n]$, the subcube of $\mathcal{P}(n)$ spanned by $A$ and $B$ consists of all subsets of $A\cup B$ that contain $A\cap B$.

nodes.name: Container
nodes.statement: A container is a subset $F\subseteq V(G)$ such that some collection $\mathcal{F}$ of containers is small ($|\mathcal{F}|=2^{o(|I_{\max}|)}$), every independent set lies in some $F\in\mathcal{F}$, and $|F|\leq(1+o(1))|I_{\max}|$.

nodes.name: Hamming distance $d(A,B)$
nodes.statement: $d(A,B):=|A\setminus B|+|B\setminus A|$ for $A,B\subseteq[n]$, equivalently the number of coordinates where the indicator strings of $A,B$ differ.

nodes.name: Hamming ball $B(A,r)$
nodes.statement: $B(A,r):=\{X\subseteq[n] : d(A,X)\leq r\}$. Its volume is $V(n,t):=\sum_{k=0}^{t}\binom{n}{k}$ for radius $t$.

nodes.name: $t$-error correcting code
nodes.statement: A family $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(n)$ is $t$-error correcting iff for every $A,B\in\mathcal{C}$ we have $d(A,B)\geq 2t+1$; equivalently, the Hamming balls $\{B(A,t):A\in\mathcal{C}\}$ are disjoint.

nodes.name: Hamming bound $H(n,t)$
nodes.statement: $H(n,t):=2^n/V(n,t)$, the Hamming bound on the size of any $t$-error correcting code.

nodes.name: Transportation distance
nodes.statement: For $(A_1,A_2),(B_1,B_2)\in\mathcal{Y}$ (pairs of disjoint $k$-subsets of $[n]$): $d((A_1,A_2),(B_1,B_2)):=\min\{|A_1\setminus B_1|+|A_2\setminus B_2|,\ |A_1\setminus B_2|+|A_2\setminus B_1|\}$.

nodes.name: $2$-$(n,k,d)$-code
nodes.statement: A collection $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{Y}$ is a $2$-$(n,k,d)$-code if the transportation distance between any two distinct elements of $\mathcal{C}$ is at least $d$.

nodes.name: $t$-intersecting family
nodes.statement: A family $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(n)$ is $t$-intersecting if $|A\cap B|\geq t$ for all $A,B\in\mathcal{A}$.

nodes.name: Random Boolean lattice $\mathcal{P}(n,p)$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{P}(n,p)$ is the random subset obtained from $\mathcal{P}(n)$ by selecting each element independently with probability $p$.

nodes.name: Symmetric chain decomposition (SCD)
nodes.statement: An SCD of $\mathcal{P}(n)$ is a partition of $\mathcal{P}(n)$ into symmetric chains: chains that for some $k\leq n/2$ contain precisely one set of each size $i\in[k,n-k]$.

nodes.name: Comparable with monochromatic difference
nodes.statement: Given a 2-colouring $R\cup W=[n]$, a pair $A,B\in\mathcal{P}(n)$ is comparable with monochromatic difference if $A\subset B$ and $B\setminus A$ is monochromatic.

nodes.name: Intersecting set-pair system (ISP-system)
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F}=\{(A_j,B_j):1\leq j\leq m\}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(N)\times\mathcal{P}(N)$ is an ISP-system with parameters $(n,N)$ if (1) $A_j\cap B_j=\emptyset$, (2) $A_j\cap B_k\neq\emptyset$ for $j\neq k$, (3) $|A_j|+|B_j|\leq n$.

nodes.name: Maximal independent set; $\mathrm{mis}(G)$
nodes.statement: An independent set $I$ of $G$ is maximal if for every $v\in V(G)\setminus I$, $I\cup\{v\}$ is not independent. $\mathrm{mis}(G)$ denotes the number of maximal independent sets.

nodes.name: Bipartite Boolean lattice graph $\mathcal{B}_{n,k}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{B}_{n,k}$ is the bipartite graph with vertex set $\binom{[n]}{k}\cup\binom{[n]}{k+1}$ and edges given by inclusion.

nodes.name: Brightwell--Katona bound $H(n,k,d)$
nodes.statement: $C(n,k,d)\leq H(n,k,d):=\frac{1}{2}\frac{n(n-1)\cdots(n-2k+d)}{(k(k-1)\cdots\lceil(d+1)/2\rceil)(k(k-1)\cdots\lfloor(d+1)/2\rfloor)}$.

nodes.name: Katona's intersection theorem value $K(n,t)$
nodes.statement: $K(n,t)=\binom{n}{\geq(n+t)/2}$ if $2\mid(n+t)$, else $K(n,t)=2\binom{n-1}{\geq(n+t-1)/2}$.

nodes.name: Sperner's theorem
nodes.statement: The largest antichain in $\mathcal{P}(n)$ has size $\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$.

nodes.name: Leader--Long: largest tilted Sperner family
nodes.statement: For coprime $p,q\in\mathbb{N}$ with $p<q$, the largest $(p,q)$-tilted Sperner family in $\mathcal{P}(n)$ has size $(q-p+o(1))\binom{n}{n/2}$.
conclusions: The largest $(p,q)$-tilted Sperner family has size $(q-p+o(1))\binom{n}{n/2}$

nodes.name: Counting tilted Sperner families
nodes.statement: Let $p,q\in\mathbb{N}$ be coprime with $p<q$. Then the number of $(p,q)$-tilted Sperner families in $\mathcal{P}(n)$ is $2^{(q-p+o(1))\binom{n}{n/2}}$.

nodes.name: Supersaturation for tilted Sperner
nodes.statement: Given $\eps>0$, there exist $\delta>0,n_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that if $n\geq n_0$ and $|\mathcal{A}|\geq(q-p+\eps)\binom{n}{n/2}$ then $\mathcal{A}$ contains $\geq\delta\binom{n}{n/2}n^{p+q}$ pairs $A,B$ with $q|A\setminus B|=p|B\setminus A|$.

nodes.name: Container lemma for tilted Sperner
nodes.statement: There is a collection $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}(n))$ with $|\mathcal{F}|=2^{o(\binom{n}{n/2})}$, every $(p,q)$-tilted Sperner family lies in some $F\in\mathcal{F}$, and $|F|\leq(q-p+o(1))\binom{n}{n/2}$.
conclusions: Container collection $\mathcal{F}$ with the three stated properties

nodes.name: Counting $t$-error correcting codes
nodes.statement: If $t=t(n)\ll\sqrt[3]{n/\log^2 n}$ then the number of $t$-error correcting codes in $\mathcal{P}(n)$ is at most $2^{H(n,t)(1+o(1))}$.

nodes.name: First supersaturation for Hamming codes
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{C}\subset\mathcal{P}(n)$ with $|\mathcal{C}|\geq H(n,t)+x$ then there are $\geq x\,n/(2t)$ pairs $A,B\in\mathcal{C}$ with $d(A,B)\leq 2t$.

nodes.name: Second supersaturation for Hamming codes (high-degree vertex)
nodes.statement: If $|\mathcal{C}|\geq 2H(n,t)$ then some $A\in\mathcal{C}$ has degree $\geq\alpha|\mathcal{C}|$ in $G[\mathcal{C}]$, where $\alpha:=n/(10tH(n,t))$.

nodes.name: Container lemma for Hamming codes
nodes.statement: For $t\ll\sqrt[3]{n/\log^2 n}$ there is a collection $\mathcal{F}$ with $|\mathcal{F}|=2^{o(H(n,t))}$, every $t$-error correcting code lies in some $F\in\mathcal{F}$, and $|F|\leq(1+o(1))H(n,t)$.
conclusions: Container collection $\mathcal{F}$ with the three stated properties

nodes.name: Counting $2$-$(n,k,2t+1)$-codes
nodes.statement: If $k=k(n)\leq n/2$ and $t=t(n)\ll\sqrt[3]{k/\log^2 n}$ then the number of $2$-$(n,k,2t+1)$-codes is at most $2^{H(n,k,2t+1)(1+o(1))}$.

nodes.name: First supersaturation for transportation codes
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{Y}$ and $|\mathcal{C}|\geq H(n,k,2t+1)+x$ then there are $\geq xk/t$ pairs $(A_1,B_1),(A_2,B_2)\in\mathcal{C}$ at transportation distance $\leq 2t$.

nodes.name: Second supersaturation for transportation codes
nodes.statement: If $|\mathcal{C}|\geq 2H(n,k,2t+1)$ then some $(A_1,B_1)\in\mathcal{C}$ has degree $\geq\alpha|\mathcal{C}|$ in $G[\mathcal{C}]$, where $\alpha:=k/(10tH(n,k,2t+1))$.

nodes.name: Container lemma for transportation codes
nodes.statement: For $k\leq n/2$ and $t\ll\sqrt[3]{k/\log^2 n}$ there is $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $\mathcal{Y}$ with $|\mathcal{F}|=2^{o(H(n,k,2t+1))}$, every $2$-$(n,k,2t+1)$-code lies in some $F$, and $|F|\leq(1+o(1))H(n,k,2t+1)$.
conclusions: Container collection $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $\mathcal{Y}$ with the three stated properties

nodes.name: Lower bound: random Katona fails for very small $p$
nodes.statement: Let $p=2^{-\Omega(\sqrt{n}\log n)}$ with $p\geq\omega(n)/2^n$ and $t=o(\sqrt{n})$. Then w.h.p. the largest $t$-intersecting family in $\mathcal{P}(n,p)$ has size $\geq(1/2+\eps)2^n p$ for some constant $\eps>0$.
conclusions: Exists $\eps>0$: w.h.p. largest $t$-intersecting family in $\mathcal{P}(n,p)$ has size $\geq(1/2+\eps)2^n p$

nodes.name: Lower bound for random Katona, $t=O(\sqrt{n})$
nodes.statement: Given $C>0$ there is $\eps>0$ such that for $p<2^{-100C\sqrt{n}\log n}$ with $p\geq\omega(n)/2^n$ and $t\leq C\sqrt{n}$, w.h.p. the largest $t$-intersecting family in $\mathcal{P}(n,p)$ has size $\geq(1+\eps)pK$, where $K=K(n,t)$.
conclusions: W.h.p. largest $t$-intersecting family in $\mathcal{P}(n,p)$ has size $\geq(1+\eps)pK$

nodes.name: Random Katona intersection theorem
nodes.statement: If $p=2^{-o(\sqrt{n}\log n)}$ and $t=o(\sqrt{n})$ then w.h.p. the largest $t$-intersecting family in $\mathcal{P}(n,p)$ has size $(1/2+o(1))2^n p$.
conclusions: W.h.p. largest $t$-intersecting family in $\mathcal{P}(n,p)$ has size $(1/2+o(1))2^n p$

nodes.name: Lower bound on $|\mathcal{A}|$
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal{A}:=\{A\in\mathcal{P}(n):n/2-a\sqrt{n}/2\leq|A|\leq n/2-a\sqrt{n}/4,|A\cap[n/2]|\geq n/4+t/2\}$ we have $|\mathcal{A}|\geq 4\eps 2^n$.

nodes.name: Edge supersaturation for intersecting families
nodes.statement: If $|\mathcal{F}|\geq\sum_{k=n/2-C\sqrt{n}}^{n}\binom{n}{k}$ then $e(G[\mathcal{F}])\geq 2^{n+(C/20)\sqrt{n}\log n}$ and $\Delta(G[\mathcal{F}])\geq 2^{(C/20)\sqrt{n}\log n}$.

nodes.name: Kleitman: number of antichains
nodes.statement: The number of antichains in $\mathcal{P}(n)$ is $A(n)=2^{\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}(1+o(1))}$.

nodes.name: Kleitman supersaturation for antichains
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(n)$ with $|\mathcal{A}|\geq\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}+x$ then $\mathcal{A}$ contains at least $(\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1)x$ comparable pairs $A\subset B$.

nodes.name: Layered supersaturation extension
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(n)$ with $|\mathcal{F}|=\binom{n}{n/2}+x$ and $N\leq|A|\leq n-N$ for all $A\in\mathcal{F}$, then $\frac{B_{\geq N}}{\binom{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+\lceil N/2\rceil}{N}}+\sum_{k=1}^{N-1}\frac{B_k}{\binom{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+\lceil k/2\rceil}{k}}\geq x$.

nodes.name: Katona--Kleitman two-coloured Sperner
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(n)$ does not contain a comparable pair with monochromatic difference (for some 2-colouring $R\cup W=[n]$) then $|\mathcal{A}|\leq\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(n)$ has no comparable pair with monochromatic difference

nodes.name: Two-coloured Sperner supersaturation
nodes.statement: Given partition $R\cup W=[n]$ and $\mathcal{F}\subset\mathcal{P}(n)$ with $|\mathcal{F}|\geq(1+\eps)\binom{n}{n/2}$, $\mathcal{F}$ contains $\geq\eps\binom{n}{n/2}n^{3/4}/4$ comparable pairs with monochromatic difference.

nodes.name: Counting two-coloured Sperner families
nodes.statement: The number of families $\mathcal{F}$ admitting a 2-colouring $R\cup W=[n]$ with no comparable pair $A,B\in\mathcal{F}$ of monochromatic difference is $2^{\binom{n}{n/2}(1+o(1))}$.

nodes.name: Bollob\'as / Griggs--Stahl--Trotter ISP-system bound
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{F}$ is an ISP-system with parameters $(n,N)$ then $|\mathcal{F}|\leq\binom{n}{n/2}$, with equality attainable when $N\geq n$.

nodes.name: Skew-Bollob\'as inequality
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}=\{(A_1,B_1),\ldots,(A_m,B_m)\}$ be ordered with (i) $|A_i|\leq a,|B_i|\leq b$, (ii) $A_i\cap B_i=\emptyset$, (iii) $A_i\cap B_j\neq\emptyset$ for $i<j$. Then $m\leq\binom{a+b}{a}$.

nodes.name: Supersaturation for ISP-systems (later disproved)
nodes.statement: Suppose $\mathcal{F}\subset\mathcal{P}(N)\times\mathcal{P}(N)$ with $|\mathcal{F}|=\binom{n}{n/2}+x$ satisfying (1) and (3). Then there are $\geq(\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1)x$ pairs $(A_i,B_i),(A_j,B_j)$ violating (2). (Note added 2018: false.)

nodes.name: No-supersaturation construction for skew-Bollob\'as
nodes.statement: Construction with $\mathcal{F}_1=\{(A,\{2,\ldots,n+1\}\setminus A):A\subset\{2,\ldots,n\},|A|=n/2\}$ and $\mathcal{F}_2=\{(A,[n]\setminus A):A\subset[n],|A|=n/2\}$ has $|\mathcal{F}|=\frac{3}{2}\binom{n}{n/2}$ but only $\frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{n/2}$ violating pairs, so straightforward containers fail.

nodes.name: Many skew-Bollob\'as families exist
nodes.statement: The number of families in $\mathcal{P}(n+1)\times\mathcal{P}(n+1)$ satisfying (i)--(iii) of the skew-Bollob\'as inequality with $a=b=n/2$ is at least $2^{1.29\binom{n}{n/2}}$.

nodes.name: Ilinca--Kahn $\mathrm{mis}(\mathcal{B}_{n,k})$ asymptotic
nodes.statement: $\log_2\mathrm{mis}(\mathcal{B}_{n,k})=(1+o(1))\binom{n-1}{k}$.

nodes.name: Ilinca--Kahn sharp $\mathrm{mis}$ conjecture (disproved)
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{mis}(\mathcal{B}_{n,k})=(1+o(1))n2^{\binom{n-1}{k}}$ as $n\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Ilinca--Kahn maximal antichain conjecture (disproved)
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{ma}(\mathcal{P}(n))=\Theta(n2^{\binom{n-1}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}})$.

nodes.name: First $\mathrm{mis}(\mathcal{B}_{n,k})$ lower bound
nodes.statement: If $|k-n/2|\leq\sqrt{n}$ then $\mathrm{mis}(\mathcal{B}_{n,k})=\Omega(n^{3/2}2^{\binom{n-1}{k}})$.

nodes.name: Improved $\mathrm{mis}(\mathcal{B}_{n,k})$ lower bound
nodes.statement: There is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that for $|k-n/2|\leq\sqrt{n}$, $\mathrm{mis}(\mathcal{B}_{n,k})\geq 2^{\binom{n-1}{k-1}+Cn^{3/2}}$.

nodes.name: Sapozhenko's question on $t$-error correcting codes
nodes.statement: Estimate $|\{\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(n):\mathcal{C}\ t\text{-error correcting}\}|$, the total number of $t$-error correcting codes in $\mathcal{P}(n)$.

nodes.name: Random Katona threshold (Question 5.1)
nodes.statement: For which values of $p$ does the largest $t$-intersecting family in $\mathcal{P}(n,p)$ have size $(1+o(1))pK(n,t)$ w.h.p.?

nodes.name: Optimal range of $t$ in Theorem 4.2 / 4.7
nodes.statement: Conjectured: the conclusions of Theorems on the number of $t$-error correcting codes / $2$-$(n,k,2t+1)$-codes should hold whenever $t\ll n/\log n$ (resp. $t\ll k/\log n$); known only for the cube-root range.

nodes.name: Kleitman--Winston graph container algorithm
nodes.statement: Iterative greedy algorithm that, given a graph $G$, an independent set $I$, and parameter $\Delta$, builds a fingerprint $S\subseteq I$ and a residual set $f(S)$ with $I\subseteq S\cup f(S)$.
output: Function value $f(S):=V(G_i)$ at termination, with $\Delta(G_i)<\Delta$ and $I\subseteq S\cup f(S)$

nodes.name: Construction $\mathcal{F}_1\cup\mathcal{F}_2$ disproving skew-Bollob\'as supersaturation
nodes.statement: Concrete pair of families $\mathcal{F}_1,\mathcal{F}_2\subseteq\mathcal{P}([n+1])^2$ with $|\mathcal{F}|=\frac{3}{2}\binom{n}{n/2}$ but only $\frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{n/2}$ violating pairs, witnessing failure of supersaturation.

nodes.name: Triple-modification construction for $\mathrm{mis}(\mathcal{B}_{n,k})$
nodes.statement: For each good triple $\T=(B,r,s)$, modify the Ilinca--Kahn induced-matching construction along a 6-cycle to obtain $|f(\T)|=2^{\binom{n-1}{k}-n+1}$ independent sets, doubling-counted at most twice.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP415.1 (tilted supersaturation)
nodes.statement: Random-permutation averaging argument: pick random ordering of $[n]$, build a chain $\mathcal{C}_\pi$ of tilted-comparable sets, bound expected intersection from below, then count good pairs via combinatorial double-counting.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP415.2 (tilted container)
nodes.statement: Apply the Kleitman--Winston container algorithm with parameter $\delta n$ to the auxiliary tilted-pair graph; combine with Lemma LP415.1 to bound the residual.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP415.3 (Hamming first supersaturation)
nodes.statement: Double-count $(X,A)$ with $d(A,X)\leq t$ via $\sum_k k|S_k|=|\mathcal{C}|V(n,t)\geq 2^n+xV(n,t)$, then bound bad pairs using $W(t,1)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP415.4 (Hamming high-degree)
nodes.statement: Double-count pairs $(X,(A,B))$ via the convexity bound $\sum_X\binom{|K_X|}{2}\geq 2^n\binom{|\mathcal{C}|V(n,t)/2^n}{2}$, then average to extract a high-degree vertex.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP415.5 (Hamming container)
nodes.statement: Run the Kleitman--Winston algorithm in two stages: large-graph stage uses Lemma LP415.4 (multiplicative shrinkage), small-graph stage uses Lemma LP415.3 (degree threshold $\eps n/4t$).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP415.6 (transport first supersaturation)
nodes.statement: Sum sizes of balls $P((A,B),k-t)$, lower-bound by $|\mathcal{Z}(k-t)|+x\binom{k}{k-t}^2$, then use $W(k-t,1)$ to count bad pairs.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP415.7 (transport high-degree)
nodes.statement: Mirrors the Hamming-codes proof: use $K_X$ over $X\in\mathcal{Z}(k-t)$ and $|\mathcal{Z}(k-t)|=H(n,k,2t+1)\binom{k}{k-t}^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP415.8 (transport container)
nodes.statement: Run two-stage Kleitman--Winston with parameter $\eps k/2t$, applying LP415.7 then LP415.6 as in the Hamming case.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP415.6 (random Katona lower bound)
nodes.statement: Build $\mathcal{A}_{\rm ex}$ from upper layers, augment with a sample $\mathcal{A}_p$ from middle layers; bound $\mathbb{E}[X]$ and use Chebyshev (Alon--Spencer Cor. 4.3.4) to concentrate.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP415.8 (random Katona upper bound)
nodes.statement: Reduce to $t=1$; build containers via the Kleitman--Winston algorithm with parameter $2^{\eps\sqrt{n}\log n}$ and use Chernoff plus Frankl--Ahlswede edge-minimisation (Claim ClP415.2).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP415.10 (Kleitman antichain supersaturation)
nodes.statement: For a random permutation $\pi$, count expected number of bad pairs in the SCD $\pi(\mathcal{X})$ via the shadow $\delta_A(B)$, comparing with the lower bound from pigeonhole.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP415.9 (Kleitman antichain count)
nodes.statement: Apply Kleitman--Winston container algorithm with parameter $\eps n/10$ to the comparability graph; supersaturation TP415.10 bounds the residual.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP415.9 (two-coloured supersaturation)
nodes.statement: Case split on $|R|$. If $|R|\leq n^{3/4}$, apply Kleitman supersaturation TP415.10 within each $\mathcal{F}_S$. Otherwise, double-count bad pairs over random permutations of pair-of-SCD decomposition.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP415.12 (two-coloured counting)
nodes.statement: Apply container method exactly as in the antichain proof using LP415.9 as supersaturation; multiply by $2^n$ choices of colouring.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition PrP415.2
nodes.statement: Use good triples $\T=(B,r,s)$ to construct collection $f(\T)$ of independent sets along a 6-cycle in $\mathcal{B}_{n,k}$; show every maximal independent set is hit at most twice.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition PrP415.3
nodes.statement: Iterate Proposition PrP415.2 on $N=Cn^{3/2}/2$ pairwise-far good triples; combine independence of modifications to get $\mathrm{mis}(\mathcal{B}_{n,k})\geq 2^{\binom{n-1}{k-1}+Cn^{3/2}}$.

nodes.name: Reduce to size-restricted $\mathcal{A}$
nodes.statement: Discard sets in $\mathcal{A}$ whose size lies outside $[n/2-C\sqrt{n},n/2+C\sqrt{n}]$, losing at most $\eps/2\binom{n}{n/2}$.

nodes.name: Choose residue class $k$
nodes.statement: By pigeonhole, exists $k\in[0,q-p-1]$ with $\sum_{i\equiv k\bmod(q-p)}|\mathcal{A}_i|\geq(1+\eps/(2(q-p)))\binom{n}{n/2}$.

nodes.name: Random ordering and chain $\mathcal{C}_\pi$
nodes.statement: Pick random permutation $\pi$ of $[n]$, define chain $C_{\pi,i}$ giving $\mathcal{C}_\pi=\{C_{\pi,i}:i\in[0,m-1]\}$ of tilted-comparable sets.

nodes.name: Lower bound on $\mathbb{E}X$
nodes.statement: Compute $\mathbb{E}|\mathcal{A}\cap\mathcal{C}_\pi|=\sum_i|\mathcal{A}_i|/\binom{n}{i}\geq 1+\eps/(2(q-p))$ using the residue-class bound.

nodes.name: Permutation count for each good pair
nodes.statement: For a good pair $A,B$, exactly $|A\cap B|!|A\setminus B|!|B\setminus A|!|\overline{A\cup B}|!$ permutations realise both as elements of $\mathcal{C}_\pi$.

nodes.name: Combine to count good pairs
nodes.statement: Combine the lower bound on $\sum_\pi\binom{\alpha(\pi)}{2}$ with the upper bound on the per-pair count to get $\geq\delta\binom{n}{n/2}n^{p+q}$ good pairs (using Fact 2.2).

nodes.name: Define auxiliary graph $G$
nodes.statement: Define $G$ on $\mathcal{P}(n)$ with $A\sim B$ iff $p|A\setminus B|=q|B\setminus A|$ or vice versa; tilted Sperner families $=$ independent sets.

nodes.name: Run Kleitman--Winston with $\Delta=\delta n$
nodes.statement: Iterate maximum-degree extraction to build $S\subseteq I$ with $|S|\leq 2^n/(\delta n)$ and $I\subseteq S\cup f(S)$.

nodes.name: Bound $|f(S)|$ via supersaturation
nodes.statement: At termination $\Delta(G_i)<\delta n$ so $e(G_i)<\delta n2^n<\delta\binom{n}{n/2}n^{p+q}$; Lemma LP415.1 forces $|V(G_i)|\leq(q-p+\eps)\binom{n}{n/2}$.

nodes.name: Verify $f$ well-defined and conclude
nodes.statement: $u$ is always picked as max-degree vertex of $G_{i-1}$, so identical $S$ from any $I,I'$ yields the same $f(S)$. Set $\mathcal{F}=\{S\cup f(S)\}$.

nodes.name: Define $K_X$ and double-count
nodes.statement: $K_X:=\{A\in\mathcal{C}:d(A,X)\leq t\}$; $\sum_k k|S_k|=|\mathcal{C}|V(n,t)\geq 2^n+xV(n,t)$.

nodes.name: Bound bad pairs via $W(t,1)$
nodes.statement: $\#\text{bad pairs}\geq\frac{1}{W(t,1)}\sum_k|S_k|\binom{k}{2}\geq xV(n,t)/W(t,1)\geq xn/(2t)$.

nodes.name: Edge-colour double count
nodes.statement: $\sum_{k=1}^{2t}W(t,k)E_k=\sum_X\binom{|K_X|}{2}$, both sides counting $(X,(A,B))$ with $d(X,A),d(X,B)\leq t$.

nodes.name: Convexity lower bound
nodes.statement: $\sum_X\binom{|K_X|}{2}\geq 2^n\binom{|\mathcal{C}|V(n,t)/2^n}{2}$ by convexity, since $|\mathcal{C}|V(n,t)/2^n\geq 2$.

nodes.name: Extract high-degree vertex
nodes.statement: Using $W(t,k)\leq W(t,1)\leq(2t/n)V(n,t)$, $E\geq|\mathcal{C}|^2V(n,t)n/(20t2^n)$, so average degree $\geq\alpha|\mathcal{C}|$.

nodes.name: Run KW with parameter $\eps n/4t$
nodes.statement: Apply graph container algorithm with degree threshold $\eps n/4t$; use first supersaturation LP415.3 to bound $|f(S)|\leq(1+\eps)H(n,t)$.

nodes.name: Stage 1: bound $|S_1|$ via LP415.4
nodes.statement: While $|V(G_{i-1})|\geq 2H(n,t)$, each step removes an $\alpha$-fraction (by LP415.4): $|S_1|\leq\log(2^n/2H(n,t))/\log(1/(1-\alpha))\leq\eps H(n,t)/(2t\log n)$.

nodes.name: Stage 2: bound $|S_2|$
nodes.statement: After $|V(G_i)|<2H(n,t)$, every step removes $\geq\eps n/4t$ vertices: $|S_2|\leq 8tH(n,t)/(\eps n)\leq\eps H(n,t)/(2t\log n)$.

nodes.name: Bound $|\mathcal{F}|$
nodes.statement: $|\mathcal{F}|\leq\binom{2^n}{\leq\eps H(n,t)/(t\log n)}\leq 2^{5\eps H(n,t)}$, completing the container construction.

nodes.name: Stage 1 (transport): apply LP415.7
nodes.statement: While $|V(G_{i-1})|\geq 2H(n,k,2t+1)$, LP415.7 gives a $\geq\alpha$ fraction shrinkage: $|S_1|\leq\eps H(n,k,2t+1)/(2t\log n)$.

nodes.name: Stage 2 (transport): apply LP415.6
nodes.statement: After threshold drops, each step removes $\geq\eps k/(2t)$ vertices: $|S_2|\leq(4t/\eps k)H(n,k,2t+1)\leq\eps H(n,k,2t+1)/(2t\log n)$.

nodes.name: Conclude container size
nodes.statement: $|\mathcal{F}|\leq 2^{20\eps H(n,k,2t+1)}$ and $|F|\leq(1+2\eps)H(n,k,2t+1)$, so the container collection works for arbitrary $\eps>0$.

nodes.name: Construct $t$-intersecting family $\mathcal{A}_{\rm ex}$
nodes.statement: Set $\mathcal{A}_{\rm ex}:=\binom{[n]}{\geq n/2+t/2}$; $|\mathcal{A}_{\rm ex}|\geq(1/2-\eps/2)2^n$ since $t=o(\sqrt{n})$.

nodes.name: Define candidate set $\mathcal{A}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}:=\{A:n/2-a\sqrt{n}/2\leq|A|\leq n/2-a\sqrt{n}/4,\ |A\cap[n/2]|\geq n/4+t/2\}$; show $|\mathcal{A}|\geq 4\eps 2^n$ via Fact 2.2.

nodes.name: Probability that $A\in\mathcal{A}_p$
nodes.statement: Bound $\#\{B\in\binom{[n]}{\geq n/2}:|A\cap B|<t\}\leq 2^{0.6a\sqrt{n}\log n}$, so $\Pr[A\in\mathcal{A}_p]\geq p(1-p)^{2^{0.6a\sqrt{n}\log n}}$.

nodes.name: Lower bound $\mathbb{E}X$
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}X\geq 4\eps 2^n p(1-p2^{0.6a\sqrt{n}\log n})\geq 3\eps p2^n$.

nodes.name: Concentrate via Chebyshev
nodes.statement: Bound $\Delta=\sum_{i\sim j}\Pr[A_i\cap A_j]\leq 2^n2^{10a\sqrt{n}\log n}p^2=o(\mathbb{E}X^2)$ to get w.h.p. $X\geq 2\eps p2^n$ by Cor.~4.3.4 of Alon--Spencer.

nodes.name: Combine $\mathcal{A}_p\cup\mathcal{A}_{{\rm ex},p}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{A}_p\cup\mathcal{A}_{{\rm ex},p}$ is $t$-intersecting w.h.p. and has size $\geq(1/2+\eps)p2^n$.

nodes.name: Reduce to $t=1$
nodes.statement: Lower bound is $(1/2+o(1))2^n p$; for upper bound, suffices to prove for intersecting ($t=1$) families since $t$-intersecting $\Rightarrow$ intersecting.

nodes.name: Apply Frankl--Ahlswede edge minimisation (Claim ClP415.2)
nodes.statement: Use Claim ClP415.2 (which follows from the Frankl--Ahlswede result) to get $\Delta(G[\mathcal{F}])\geq 2^{(C/20)\sqrt{n}\log n}$ when $|\mathcal{F}|\geq\sum_{n/2-C\sqrt{n}}^{n}\binom{n}{k}$.

nodes.name: Build containers
nodes.statement: Apply Kleitman--Winston with parameter $2^{\eps\sqrt{n}\log n}$ to $G$ (disjointness graph). $|F|\leq(1/2+2\gamma)2^n$ and $\log|\mathcal{F}|\leq 2^{n-(\eps/2)\sqrt{n}\log n}$.

nodes.name: Apply Chernoff over each container
nodes.statement: $\Pr[|F\cap\mathcal{P}(n,p)|\geq(1/2+4\gamma)2^n p]\leq 2e^{-\gamma^2 2^n p/2}$; union bound over $\mathcal{F}$ controls all containers w.h.p.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Every intersecting family lies in some $F\in\mathcal{F}$, hence has size $\leq(1/2+\delta)2^n p$ w.h.p.

nodes.name: Reduce to $\emptyset,[n]\notin\mathcal{A}$
nodes.statement: WLOG $\emptyset,[n]\notin\mathcal{A}$; this contributes only $O(1)$ to the count.

nodes.name: Random SCD $\pi(\mathcal{X})$
nodes.statement: Fix SCD $\mathcal{X}$, pick $\pi\in S_n$ uniformly; $\pi(\mathcal{X})$ is also a SCD with $\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ chains.

nodes.name: Shadow argument bounds chain probability
nodes.statement: For each ordered pair $(A,B)\in\mathcal{P}$, $|\delta_A(B)|\geq\binom{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, so the probability that a chain of $\pi(\mathcal{X})$ contains both is $\leq 1/(\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1)$.

nodes.name: Pigeonhole and conclude
nodes.statement: Pigeonhole gives $\geq x$ bad pairs in $\pi(\mathcal{X})$; expectation $\leq|\mathcal{P}|/(\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1)$, so $|\mathcal{P}|\geq(\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1)x$.

nodes.name: Apply KW with $\Delta=\eps n/10$
nodes.statement: Run the Kleitman--Winston algorithm on the comparability graph with parameter $\eps n/10$; supersaturation TP415.10 bounds the residual to $(1+\eps)\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$.

nodes.name: Count containers
nodes.statement: $|\mathcal{F}|\leq\binom{2^n}{\leq 10\cdot 2^n/(\eps n)}\leq 2^{20\cdot 2^n\log n/(\eps n)}=2^{o(\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor})}$.

nodes.name: Case A: $|R|\leq n^{3/4}$
nodes.statement: Apply Kleitman supersaturation TP415.10 to each $\mathcal{F}_S=\{A\subseteq W:A\cup S\in\mathcal{F}\}$, summing over $S\subseteq R$ to get $\geq\eps\binom{n}{n/2}n/6$ bad pairs.

nodes.name: Case B: $|R|,|W|\geq n^{3/4}$
nodes.statement: Drop monochromatic / containing-$R$/$W$ elements (cost $\leq\eps/2\binom{n}{n/2}$); use product-of-SCDs of $\mathcal{P}(R),\mathcal{P}(W)$ and random $\pi\in S_{|R|}\times S_{|W|}$.

nodes.name: Pair-of-SCD pigeonhole
nodes.statement: Show $\sum_{X,Y}\min\{|X|,|Y|\}=\binom{n}{n/2}$, so each subfamily of size $\binom{n}{n/2}+1$ creates at least one bad pair in any pair-of-SCDs.

nodes.name: Random shadow bound $\leq 2/n^{3/4}$
nodes.statement: For each bad pair $(A,B)$, the probability $(A\cap R, B\cap R)\subseteq\pi_R(\mathcal{B}_R)$ is $\leq\max\{2/|R|,2/|W|\}\leq 2/n^{3/4}$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Comparing the $\geq x$ pair lower bound with the $\leq 2/n^{3/4}$ per-pair probability gives $\geq\eps\binom{n}{n/2}n^{3/4}/4$ bad pairs.

nodes.name: Set up induced matching $M$
nodes.statement: $M:=\{(C,C\cup\{1\}):1\notin C, |C|=k\}$ is an induced matching of size $\binom{n-1}{k-1}$ in $\mathcal{B}_{n,k}$.

nodes.name: Construct $f(\T)$ from good triple
nodes.statement: For good triple $\T=(B,r,s)$ define $D(\T),U(\T)$ and edges $e,f$; $f(\T)$ is the family of independent sets fixing $B^r,B^1_s$ and respecting $M$, with $|f(\T)|=2^{\binom{n-1}{k}-n+1}$.

nodes.name: Each $I\in\mathcal{F}$ arises from exactly two good triples
nodes.statement: Edges $e,f$ form unique 6-cycle in $\mathcal{B}_{n,k}$; the only other triple producing $I$ is $\T'=(B^r_s,s,r)$.

nodes.name: Count good triples and conclude
nodes.statement: $\#\text{good triples}=\binom{n-1}{k}k(n-k-1)=\Omega(n^{3/2}2^n)$, so $\mathrm{mis}(\mathcal{B}_{n,k})\geq|\mathcal{F}|/2=\Omega(n^{3/2}2^{\binom{n-1}{k}})$.

nodes.name: Initialise $G_0,S$
nodes.statement: Set $G_0:=G$, $S:=\emptyset$, fix arbitrary total order $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ of $V(G)$.

nodes.name: Choose max-degree vertex
nodes.statement: At Step $i$, let $u$ be the vertex of maximum degree in $G_{i-1}$, ties broken by the fixed total order.

nodes.name: Branch on membership and degree
nodes.statement: If $u\notin I$: $G_i:=G_{i-1}\setminus\{u\}$. Else if $u\in I$ and $\deg_{G_{i-1}}(u)\geq\Delta$: add $u$ to $S$, $G_i:=G_{i-1}\setminus(\{u\}\cup N_G(u))$. Else if $u\in I$ and $\deg_{G_{i-1}}(u)<\Delta$: set $f(S):=V(G_i)$ and terminate.

nodes.name: Return $(S,f(S))$
nodes.statement: Return $S$ with $|S|\leq|V|/\Delta$ and $f(S)=V(G_i)$ where $\Delta(G_i)<\Delta$ and $I\subseteq S\cup f(S)$.
